artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan reconciling index.schema.json into one authority, adding advisory Rules T/U to check-extension-docs.sh with a fixture test, correcting both competing prose examples, bringing Tier-1 always-load from 996L to a predicted 334L, and creating four named follow-on tasks for the deferred bulk migrations.

metadata.scope_decision: Adopted the research's split recommendation with the boundary moved: Phase A plus the Tier-1 demotion, the extensions/README.md correction, and the EXTENSION.md length check land here; four follow-on tasks (index_entries_schema_migration, meta_catchall_decomposition, extension_md_slim_down, promote_schema_gates_to_hard) carry the deferred bulk work and two of the three VERIFICATION BAR lines.
metadata.research_correction: Rule T cannot reuse INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE (already defaults hard; Rules R/S depend on that). Plan introduces sibling SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE defaulting advisory.

memory_candidates.content: In check-extension-docs.sh, a new lint rule whose codebase is not yet remediated must get its OWN gate-severity variable, never reuse an existing one. INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE defaults to 'hard' because Rules R/S landed after their remediation was complete; routing a new pre-remediation rule through it would either hard-fail 14 of 19 extensions on day one or silently demote R/S. The established pattern is a sibling variable defaulting 'advisory' with its own reporter function (mirroring index_truth_report), promoted to 'hard' in a later dedicated task once the migration it gates has landed. ORPHAN_GATE_MODE -> INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE is the precedent; both carry comments documenting the promotion. Generalizes: gate-severity variables are per-remediation-timeline, not per-check-family.
